# Lead the multi-window article with preserved panel state

## Context
Tobi identified a preview-level ambiguity in the published title “Multi-window web apps without syncing state”: it can suggest that state is not maintained, while the intended benefit is that filters and scrolling survive a panel moving between windows. The same title is retained in the Engine source and portal listing.

## The Problem
The headline leads with an eliminated implementation task. A reader who sees only a preview must infer the preserved user experience. The article's own opening confirms the same live object, but starts with SharedWorker mechanics.

## The Architectural Reality
Design authority: the operator's 2026-10-18 clarification is “tear out a tab and state is automatically KEPT.” `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsWindows.md` documents same-instance/store/scroll continuity and selection through tear-out and return. The article is `learn/blog/a-workspace-that-can-leave-its-window.md`; its manual title is in `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json`. The similarly named Dock Layouts benefits article is a different post.

## The Fix
Lead with moving web-app panels while preserving their state. Make the first paragraph name the concrete grid result, followed by the shared App Worker explanation. Align the portal title. Preserve the article ID/path, byline, diagrams, examples and technical body. Supply matching title/subtitle copy for the operator's Medium edit.

## Contract Ledger
| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs/evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Headline/preview/portal label | Operator's clarity correction; existing blog implication check | State preservation is explicit at preview level | Existing URL and technical content retained | Matched source diff, portal JSON check and editorial reads |
| Generated SEO and Medium publication | Existing generator/publication ownership | SEO derives from source; Medium copy prepared for operator | No direct generated-file edit or autonomous publication | Handoff copy and human merge/publish |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Headline explicitly communicates the retained-state benefit when read alone; the opening scopes it to moving a panel between browser windows.
- [ ] Grid filter, selection and scroll continuity are concrete; no general persistence, crash recovery or zero-message promise is introduced.
- [ ] Source H1 and portal title agree; portal JSON parses; article URL/byline/body remain intact.
- [ ] Matching Medium title/subtitle are provided for review. Two editorial/model reads include a different family before shipping, per blog-post guidance.

## Out of Scope
No runtime change, title/slug migration, new workflow or skill rule, broader blog rewrite, automated social posting, or claim that this ambiguity caused the observed traffic outcome.
